research.title: Artificial Intelligence Driven Design and Geometry Optimization in Additive Manufacturing
research.venue: National High School Journal of Science (NHSJS)
research.summary: A structured literature review of 19 studies (2018–2026) on how AI actually supports additive-manufacturing design decisions.
research.outcome: Thematic synthesis identified four connected roles for AI in AM design: accelerating design search, generating candidate geometries, coordinating decisions across structural scales, and folding manufacturing- and process-aware constraints into optimization.
research.motivation: AM design and geometry optimization are bottlenecked by repeated simulation, very large design spaces, and manufacturing constraints that most optimizers ignore.
research.method: Scopus as the primary database with Google Scholar for citation tracing; screened 2018–2026 publications down to 19 core studies; compared them across AI method, AM process, geometry type, validation approach, performance metrics, and reported limitations.
research.findings: Key gaps remain: limited datasets, weak generalization testing, low interpretability, limited process adaptivity, and underdeveloped industrial qualification standards.

files.href: assets/docs/ai-driven-am/Artificial Intelligence Driven Design and Geometry Optimization in Additive Manufacturing Recent Advances and Future Directions.docx

research.title: Additive Manufacturing of an Anthropomorphic Hand using Force Resistive Sensors for Object Detection
research.venue: Journal of Future Science and Engineering (JFSE)
research.summary: A multimaterial 3D-printed robotic hand with film pressure sensors that identifies what it is holding at 98.1% accuracy.
research.outcome: A random forest model trained on 4,500 rows and tested on 1,000 rows classified four objects from force-sensor input at 98.1% accuracy — showing AM plus low-cost force resistive sensors can produce a bioinspired hand with object detection.
research.motivation: Current robotic hands are limited in grip-force sensitivity and cost. A clinically prescribable, commercially available prosthetic can cost upwards of $20,000 USD.
research.method: Multimaterial FDM printing — PLA for the fingers and arm, TPU for the joints and palm — with force resistive sensors integrated to read pressure during grasp. Training data was collected by repeatedly grasping four distinct objects.
research.findings: Accurate object detection from grasp pressure alone opens paths into adaptive grasp, soft robotics, smart prosthetics, human-skin biomimicry, and material-aware computer vision.

files.label: Full manuscript (PDF)
files.href: assets/docs/anthropomorphic-hand/Additive Manufacturing of an Anthropomorphic Hand using Force Resistive Sensors for Object Detection.pdf

research.title: Measure Before You Reconstruct: Remote Measurement of Residual-Limb Circumference from Sparse Smartphone Silhouettes
research.summary: A remote prosthetic-socket sizing pipeline that measures limb circumference from a handful of calibrated phone photos — no dense 3D reconstruction needed.
research.outcome: Applying Cauchy's projection formula to calibrated smartphone silhouettes hit 97.5–99.8% spectral accuracy across 33 OpenLimbTT models (validated by Fourier analysis), while eliminating COLMAP's dense-reconstruction overhead. Benchmarked against VGGT to identify failure modes.
research.motivation: e-NABLE volunteers fit recipients on the other side of the world from photos. Better remote sizing means better-fitting devices for the Uganda and West Bank cases our chapter works on.
research.method: Cauchy-based silhouette measurement algorithm with perspective corrections; Fourier analysis for spectral validation against the OpenLimbTT model set.
research.findings: Measuring directly from silhouettes beats reconstructing geometry first, for this task.

research.title: Evaluating Radicalization through Autism Diagnosis Criteria and Media Addiction
research.venue: UCSB Summer Research Academies, Track 12 “Digital Brains”
research.summary: A 4-week study asking which specific autism diagnostic traits — not autism as a monolith — relate to radicalization susceptibility.
research.outcome: Extremism correlated most with circumscribed interests; violent extremism correlated most with sensory/motor deficiencies. Problematic media use was not a significant moderating factor.
research.motivation: Existing work either treats autistic populations as homogenous or relies on narrow journalistic case studies, leaving no usable foundation for prevention programs.
research.method: Ritvo Autism Asperger Diagnostic Scale–Revised for autism symptomatology, the Problematic Media Use Measure for digital media addiction, and the Extremism Scale plus the Pro-violence and Illegal Acts in Relation to Extremism Scale for radicalization outcomes.
research.findings: Results are meant as a foundation for informed, trait-specific radicalization prevention support systems rather than blanket assumptions.

projects.title: Big Hands e-NABLE Fremont

projects.outcome: Coordinated with the World Action Fund to donate 15 custom prostheses to recipients in the West Bank and Uganda, with 40+ Ugandan cases in development. projects.motivation: A clinically prescribed prosthetic can run past $20,000. e-NABLE's open-source designs and a printer get a working device to a kid for the cost of filament — the bottleneck is volunteers who can actually design, fit, and ship them.
projects.role: Founded and lead the chapter: technical, finance, and social media teams; recipient intake; measurement and fitting; device validation; donor outreach.
projects.detail: Led development and dissemination of amputation-specific finger prosthetics, transhumeral prosthetics, and cosmetic covers for the wider e-NABLE community. Works with the United e-NABLE Coalition on Uganda cases and partners with the World Action Fund for delivery.

projects.title: Kinetic Energy Harvesting Shoe Sole
projects.subtitle: Rotary Young Innovators 3D Printing Challenge finalist · 2025
projects.summary: A 3D-printed shoe sole with embedded piezoelectric discs that harvests the energy of walking into a rechargeable battery.
projects.outcome: The prototype measurably stored harvested energy: 14.48 V peak open-circuit output under simulated footsteps, and a 0.009–0.013 V battery rise over a 30-minute walk, confirmed across two independent battery discharge experiments.
projects.motivation: Kinetic energy from human movement is abundant and almost entirely wasted. Capturing even a fraction of it is a step away from fossil-fuel reliance — and it rewards walking.
projects.role: Co-designed the project with Kevin Xia: sole CAD, electrical design, and the experimental protocol.
projects.detail: The printed sole houses 12 × 27 mm piezoelectric discs feeding a full-wave Schottky bridge rectifier (1N5819), a 134N3P lithium charging/protection module, and an 18650 cell with a 5 V boost converter for USB output. Three experiments measured open-circuit AC voltage, rectified DC voltage, and accumulated battery energy, with energy computed from Joule's law over timed discharge intervals. Iterating from 6 discs in parallel to 12 in series raised output and cut forward voltage drop from 0.7–1.0 V to 0.3–0.4 V.

projects.title: SoliC — Solar Panel Self-Cleaning System
projects.subtitle: Conrad Challenge Innovator · 2024–2025
projects.summary: A passive solar-panel cleaning system combining a dew collector with super-hydrophobic and super-hydrophilic panel coatings.
projects.outcome: Recognized as a Conrad Challenge 2024–2025 Innovator.
projects.motivation: Dust on panels quietly destroys solar yield, and washing them costs water and labor — especially wrong in the dry, dusty places solar works best.
projects.role: Product designer and video maker. Invented and developed the dew collector, the system's major innovation; contributed to adopting the hydrophobic/hydrophilic coating approach.
